title: workload.draft input
description: Draft compilation for the workload.draft operation. R2: the draft is a revisable private artifact (a generated vault page plus the typed result); it publishes and launches nothing. Compiles the caller's answers against the strict new-workload skeleton contract and the published registry: every reference (seat, project, gateway lane, memory namespace) must resolve to enabled declarations, the image reference must be fully qualified and digest-pinned, and every answer must satisfy the skeleton's declared grammar. Absent answers come back as the declared clarification list with the skeleton contract's own meanings; a complete answer set returns the exact canonical declaration and its blake3 digest — the selector the operator's publish approval binds. All values are caller-provided untrusted data; no credential, seat authority, or model override ever travels in arguments.

profileId.description: Registry id of the new workload profile; must not collide with any existing registry object.

description.description: The pod's role in one sentence.

enabled.description: Whether the profile is enabled after publication.

seat.description: Existing enabled seat the pod agent runs as.

project.description: Existing enabled project inside the seat's project_scope.

gatewayLane.description: Gateway route lane declared by an enabled provider; the declared model choice.

allowHosts.description: Allowlisted bare egress hostnames; the pod may reach exactly these and nothing else. Empty: no site at all (DNS only; an agent still reaches its model gateway).

stream.description: Whether the pod browser surface streams to the owner.

statePath.description: Absolute in-pod mount path of the per-pod state volume. Omit it: the deployment's pinned workload image supplies it.

stateStorage.description: Persistent storage quantity for the per-pod state volume (for example 2Gi); the custody layer requests exactly this.

exportPodPath.description: Absolute in-pod path of the exported folder. Omit it: the deployment's pinned workload image supplies it.

exportHostFolder.description: Absolute host folder of the explicit export.

briefText.description: Pod task brief injected into every agent turn; declaration text, never runtime state.

deadlineSeconds.description: Hard lifetime of one run in seconds; the pod is ended after it, whatever it is doing.

memoryNamespace.description: atlas.<subtree> namespace inside the bound seat's brain_scope; memory is untrusted data, never authority.

expectedRegistryRevision.description: Optional re-draft base pin: the registry revision this draft's answers were compiled against (provenance base); a mismatch is a typed stale-scope refusal.

harness.description: script: the pod runs scriptCommand in imageReference and no agent (no gateway lane, memory, display). omp or omitted: an agent pod on the platform image.

imageReference.description: A script pod's image: "platform" (Odin's deployed workload image) or fully qualified and pinned by @sha256 manifest digest. Agent pods omit it (they run "platform").

scriptCommand.description: A script pod's command, argv form, run inside the image.

placement.description: Node capabilities the pod needs (registry node capabilities such as cuda, gpu, cfd, scrape, embed).

mode.description: job: finite, ends at deadlineSeconds. service: long-lived, restarted on failure, ended by a stop; declares no deadlineSeconds.

monitoringCadenceSeconds.description: How often code reads the pod's newest `ODIN-STATUS {json}` stdout line; with watchdogs.

slice.description: The slice of the seat that handles the finding (kubert-ops for Kubert).

watchdogs.description: Code-evaluated alerts over the pod's ODIN-STATUS counters; zero model calls while healthy.

progress.description: Anti-stuck: the ODIN-STATUS counter whose growth is the pod's useful progress (a repeated value or heartbeat is not). Declare with stallSeconds and recovery.

stallSeconds.description: Anti-stuck: how long the pod may run without useful progress; at least two monitoring reads.

recovery.description: Anti-stuck ladder: when the pod stalls the kernel authorizes one step at a time — restart_worker (its seat restarts it) up to max_attempts, then escalate (an incident to Colin).

tools.description: Host capabilities the pod's agent may call — a subset of its seat's tools (e.g. memory.remember); a pod never launches pods, asks seats or creates. Omitted: none.
